governanceNotes: The nutritional effect direction is subtype-heterogeneous (early vs late dumping) per the cited systematic review; both directions are recorded so the human verifier sees the full picture.
Dumping syndrome is itself a postoperative complication; attribution versus the surgery's intended effect is an individual determination.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The international consensus defines dietary adjustment as the agreed first treatment step, making symptom-driven caloric management inherent to the syndrome (Scarpellini 2020); the management review documents continuous enteral feeding as necessary for treatment-refractory cases (van Beek 2017; Tack 2025), and the bariatric systematic review found late dumping promotes higher caloric intake while early dumping drives food avoidance (D'hoedt 2023).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the direction of the nutritional effect is heterogeneous by subtype (early-dumping food avoidance versus late-dumping increased intake per D'hoedt 2023), the syndrome itself is a postoperative complication rather than an independent disease process, and weight loss attributable to the underlying surgery, malignancy, or the intended bariatric effect must be separated from dumping-specific nutritional harm; the D'hoedt review found no significant dumping-to-degree-of-weight-loss relationship.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized avoidance-malnutrition pathway: rapid gastric emptying produces postprandial vasomotor and gastrointestinal symptoms that patients manage by restricting meal size and avoiding carbohydrate-dense foods; over time the restriction and malabsorptive transit reduce total caloric and micronutrient intake, presenting clinically as involuntary weight loss and protein-energy malnutrition. How much of any patient's malnutrition is dumping-specific versus surgery-intended is individual and unquantified.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Early- and late-dumping phenotypes move caloric intake in opposite directions; the bariatric-surgery population's weight loss is partly the intended effect and cannot be attributed to dumping without individual dietary documentation; the consensus evidence is expert-opinion and management-class rather than cohort prevalence; malnutrition must meet validated screening criteria.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented dumping syndrome after gastric/esophageal/bariatric surgery with symptomatic food-avoidance or caloric-restriction pattern; validated malnutrition screening (e.g., GLIM criteria); weight and laboratory trend chronology; exclusion of recurrence, stricture, or independent causes of weight loss; dietitian assessment
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Intended weight-loss effect of bariatric surgery
Anastomotic stricture or small-bowel bacterial overgrowth
Post-surgical taste change and food intolerance

evidenceGaps: Documented dumping syndrome after gastric/esophageal/bariatric surgery with symptomatic food-avoidance or caloric-restriction pattern; validated malnutrition screening (e.g., GLIM criteria); weight and laboratory trend chronology; exclusion of recurrence, stricture, or independent causes of weight loss; dietitian assessment
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the dietary-management burden is built into first-line care and refractory cases require enteral support, but the nutritional direction is subtype-heterogeneous and confounded by the surgical indication itself; no causal claim is forced.

sourceReferences.citation: Scarpellini E, Arts J, Karamanolis G, et al. International consensus on the diagnosis and management of dumping syndrome. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2020 Aug;16(8):448-466. PMID 32457534.
sourceReferences.note: Delphi international consensus (18 experts, 62 statements): dietary adjustment is the agreed first treatment step; decreased gastric volume capacity and rapid nutrient passage to the small bowel are pathophysiologically relevant.

sourceReferences.citation: van Beek AP, Emous M, Laville M, Tack J. Dumping syndrome after esophageal, gastric or bariatric surgery: pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management. Obes Rev. 2017 Jan;18(1):68-85. PMID 27749997.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review: surgical re-intervention or continuous enteral feeding may be necessary for treatment-refractory dumping syndrome - the refractory-nutrition-support anchor.

sourceReferences.citation: D'hoedt A, Vanuytsel T. Dumping syndrome after bariatric surgery: prevalence, pathophysiology and role in weight reduction - a systematic review. Acta Gastroenterol Belg. 2023 Jul-Sep;86(3):417-427. PMID 37814558.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review: early dumping can become a tool to maintain strict dietary patterns, but late dumping is detrimental and promotes overall higher caloric intake; no significant dumping-to-weight-loss relationship shown - the directionality guard.
